Sample.evidence_source: [/page/3/Text/6] The empirical categories that emerged from the speeches and stories of the people interviewed (men and women) who attempted suicide or had persistent suicidal ideation are now presented – the categories that emerged from the empirical data, and are subject to superimposition and many other interactions, since this is a complex subject – are: (1) the 'nowhere' situation of the subject; (2) non-acceptance of losses; (3) suffering due to ungratefulness of family members; (4) a sense of existential uselessness; and (5) re-signification of the situations that generate the suicide-related conduct.
